 Inside the final days of Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum’s tenure as Celtics teammates
 Within the Celtics organization, there appears to be a sense of relief that the tension is gone.
 Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown had plenty of success together for nine seasons with Boston. Erin Clark/The Boston Globe 
 By Gary Washburn, The Boston Globe 
 November 13, 2026

 The final encounter between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown as Celtics was fitting. It occurred in late June at the Cannes Sports Beach Event afterparty in the French Riviera, which both players coincidentally attended on the eve of Brown’s trade to the 76ers .
 When informed that Tatum was in the vicinity, Brown asked to share a VIP table with Hall of Famer Carmelo Anthony, indicating it might be best to hang out with him and his group instead.
 The silence and lack of interaction between the two Celtics greats ― who spent nine seasons together, won a championship, and reached another NBA Finals ― was an apt end to their tenure as teammates. Brown was on the trading block, Tatum had stayed out of the situation, and their near-decade-long partnership was about to end without a final conversation.
 Advertisement: 
 “I thought [Brown] felt awkward about something going on,” Anthony told the Globe. “He didn’t know what was going on at the time. I know JT was on the other side. I know Jaylen [wanted to speak with Jayson] but he didn’t know what to do. I just told him, ‘Why don’t you just go over there to JT?’
 “He was like, ‘Man, I don’t know where we are at. Do you mind if I just stay here?’ I was like, ‘Of course.’ ”
 This account is based on interviews with multiple people with knowledge of the Celtics organization’s inner workings and familiarity with the Tatum-Brown relationship. Most were granted anonymity to allow them to speak candidly.
 Advertisement: 
 Opposite personalities
 A relationship built on mutual respect and admiration deteriorated as the Celtics made clear years ago that Tatum was their No. 1 cornerstone and preferred superstar. That distinction created a wedge between Brown and the team that ended unceremoniously with his stunning trade in early July.
 The accord between the two superstars had been dissected and questioned for years. But the two All-Stars always enjoyed a respectful bond on the floor and a polite friendship off it. Tatum, a father of two, has a close circle and keeps a low profile in Boston.
 Brown has spoken at MIT and Harvard, occupies his offseason with trips to places such as Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and China. He’s also active in the National Basketball Players Association and outspoken on political issues. When he signed his unprecedented five-year, $304 million contract , he said his primary goal was to shrink the wealth gap between Boston’s Black and white communities.
 They are dramatically different personalities, but on the court they worked to align, maintained a healthy respect for one another, and realized the road to ultimate success would be easier together.
 However, it became apparent Tatum was the unquestioned face of the franchise. The Celtics made his comfort a priority, treasured his skill set, elevated him to the starting lineup at age 19, and made him untouchable in trade discussions.
 Advertisement: 
 Jayson Tatum (30 points) and Jaylen Brown (20 points) helped the Celtics blow out the 76ers in Game 4. – Danielle Parhizkaran/Globe Staff 
 The front office and coaching staff viewed Tatum as an indispensable part of their culture. Brown, lacking Tatum’s pure basketball skill set, would always be the second priority, regardless of how well he played in Tatum’s absence . Either Brown accepted that reality, or the Celtics would react accordingly.
 Brown has always believed he has not received the respect he deserves. He often brings up being booed in Boston on draft night in 2016 when Celtics fans weren’t familiar with his name or game. He has been heavily criticized for his ballhandling miscues, turnovers, and missed free throws in losses. His perceived benching in 2018 in favor of a less-than-100 percent Gordon Hayward irritated and motivated him.
 Brown was left off the 2024 Olympic team despite having just helped Boston to a championship, and Team USA offered no real explanation besides he wasn’t a “good fit.” He spent years caught in trade rumors, part of discussions for Anthony Davis, Kawhi Leonard, and Kevin Durant ― many of which were real.
 While the Celtics quickly signed Tatum to a maximum contract when he became eligible in July 2024, they took weeks to negotiate a similar deal with Brown in 2023 . Brown never forgot those slights, though he felt his 2025-26 season would earn him more organizational equity.
 Advertisement: 
 The increasing lack of on-court chemistry and Brown’s disappointing analytical numbers contributed to the Celtics pursuing the controversial trade. Sources say the front office felt the two-headed wing arsenal of Tatum and Brown had simply become a relic.
 There was a belief inside the organization that the Celtics were incapable of winning another championship with the pairing. They were too similar and too predictable in the fourth quarter, when they would take turns trying to score against ramped-up defenses while their teammates watched. Their lack of success in the New York series in 2025 and the devastating Philadelphia series loss in the first round in May cemented the organization’s thinking.
 Front office makes a choice
 Brown’s individual success during Tatum’s absence last season only exacerbated the issue. Coming off a career year, the five-time All-Star naturally desired a maximum two-year extension, and anything less would be considered an insult. Brown’s All-NBA status qualified him for a two-year, $142 million extension, meaning the Celtics would have to commit to maximum salaries for Brown and Tatum for the long term, ensuring that two players in their 30s would account for 70 percent of their salary cap.
 When the front office decided the effectiveness of the Tatum-Brown combination had waned, and Tatum was set to reassume his status as the No. 1 option, the Celtics decided to move on. Ideally, the superstars could have discussed their future together in Boston and perhaps made a pact to take less money so the team could afford a stronger supporting cast.
 Advertisement: 
 That discussion never happened. According to multiple sources, Brown and Tatum were asked to talk about their roles and partnership before Tatum returned from his Achilles injury in March. They were left alone in a room to talk, but it remains unclear what was said and whether it had any impact on their relationship.
 When Tatum returned March 6 against the Mavericks , he was introduced last in the starting lineup at TD Garden, a traditional sign of respect for the team’s best player. Brown apparently accepted the move, despite having been introduced last during Tatum’s absence.
 He never received that honor again.
 “It’s unfortunate that [their issues] got to the public,” said Rockets coach Ime Udoka , who led the Celtics to the Finals in 2021-22. “Handle it between each other. Being there and being a part of it, it’s always somewhat been a narrative. But they had a lot of success together. Should be able to talk that out and not worry what everybody else is thinking, their opinions and narratives.”
 Udoka said the Tatum-Brown dynamic wasn’t the primary issue during that season.
 “It wasn’t a ‘them’ thing, it was a team thing in general, players they had prior. A lot of ‘your turn, my turn’ and it wasn’t just those two. They had a lot of great scorers over the years. My thing was trying to get them to work together and understand the attention they draw and how they can play off each other. What I always said was any team in the league that’s criticizing or making statements would love to have both. You’ve seen the success they had and got a championship from it.”
 Advertisement: 
 Part of the reason the Celtics were ready to move on from Brown was the perception that he would become more demanding about his role after earning All-NBA honors following his best statistical season. The franchise knew it faced a difficult decision regarding a potential breakup, and the final two playoff eliminations only served as confirmation.
 Brown never asked for a trade, but once informed the Celtics were shopping him, he submitted a list of his preferred destinations and teams he preferred not to play for. Philadelphia was on neither list.
 According to NBA sources, Brown was interested in the Nets, but Brooklyn management was wary because of his past support of Kyrie Irving during Irving’s controversial tenure with the team, which included a suspension over sharing posts on social media containing antisemitic tropes.
 Brown’s recent statements suggest he believes Tatum could have approached the front office about keeping his longtime partner but chose not to intervene. Tatum has never disparaged Brown publicly, but those in the organization noticed their relationship began to change after the 2024 NBA Finals .
 The fact Brown won both the Eastern Conference finals MVP and NBA Finals MVP elevated his status around the league but not in the Celtics’ front office. Some within the organization wanted to make wholesale changes after the championship, knowing the team was aging, salaries would become a factor, and the team’s style of play could eventually lose its effectiveness.
 Jaylen Brown (center) hoists the MVP trophy following Game 5 of the NBA Finals in 2024. – Barry Chin/Globe Staff 
 But president of basketball operations Brad Stevens decided to run it back, and then Tatum tore his Achilles in the 2025 conference semifinals against the Knicks — a series the running-on-fumes Celtics likely would have lost anyway.
 Advertisement: 
 With Tatum rehabilitating, Brown took the leadership reins and led the Celtics to 56 wins . Boston earned the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs and all appeared well when Tatum returned, until they lost chemistry and blew a potential clinching Game 5 of the first-round series against the 76ers.
 Brown was apparently irritated when he learned ― while on his way to TD Garden ― that Tatum would miss the decisive Game 7 . The Celtics and coach Joe Mazzulla had reported in the two previous days that Tatum would play in perhaps the most important game since the 2024 Finals. Instead, Tatum was a late scratch. Brown then criticized Mazzulla’s rotational decisions following the loss but also called Tatum the team’s “best player.”
 Two months later, the Tatum-Brown era was over.
 Bitter feelings linger
 Their bond has since severed, with Brown tossing social media barbs and faintly disguised criticism of Tatum’s lack of support during their years together. Tatum, meanwhile, appears ready to move on , not angry with the trade but more bothered that Brown was shipped to a division rival.
 The Celtics’ front office did not keep Tatum informed on the Brown trade talks. It’s their philosophy that star players should not be involved in personnel decisions involving teammates. The fact Tatum stayed out of it appeared to make Brown more isolated. He felt like a man on an island.
 Former Celtics player Evan Turner, a Boston assistant under Stevens in 2020-21, said he’s never seen personal issues between Tatum and Brown.
 Advertisement: 
 “When people are beefing, they don’t speak to each other,” Turner said. ”I’ve sat there and never said, ‘These two don’t like each other.’ I’ve never seen any moment like that. I paid attention when they walked into the building, they acknowledged each other first. There was a heavy level of respect.
 “And when [people] say they weren’t friends, Jaylen is damn near like Iron Man. That man could be possibly doing anything. One day he’s learning salsa, the next day he’s breaking down science, the next day he’s throwing a parade. I don’t think he has time to have friends. They never said they disliked each other. There was never any ill will. And even with Jayson coming out and giving a statement, he waved the white flag and said, ‘I don’t have any problems [with Jaylen].’ ”
 “It’s tough,” former Celtic Marcus Smart said of the broken bond. “I do feel bad for those guys, my brothers, man. Been through a lot of wars, battles with them. I know the work they both put in and it’s unfortunate that it’s come to this because those are two really good guys. I think any team, any coach, any organization, to have either one would be the right decision.
 “To have both is a luxury, right? But [the Celtics] made the decision that they made. Unfortunately this is a business first and we sometimes get caught up in the relationships we build, but it’s a business and the business side ruined a lot of things, a relationship. Hopefully they can mend it and hopefully they can get back to letting basketball be basketball.”
 Advertisement: 
 The Celtics’ brass hopes Brown can eventually resolve his feelings toward the franchise and appreciate his 10 successful years in Boston, but no one expects that reconciliation soon. The feelings are too raw. Brown still appears confused about the trade and believes it epitomizes the lack of appreciation for his contributions to the franchise’s success.
 Celtics players Jayson Tatum (left) and Paul George. – Meleck Eldahshoury for The Boston Globe 
 Within the Celtics organization, there appears to be a sense of relief that the tension is gone. Tatum is the unquestioned leader. Paul George reiterated he’s in Boston to make life easier for Tatum as the second option , and appears rejuvenated with the new venue and fresh opportunity.
 The front office fully realizes the risk of the move, especially since Brown is fitting in well in Philadelphia. But management is ecstatic with George’s production, pleased with their future financial flexibility and two first-round picks, and optimistic about eventually finding a cheaper and younger second option alongside Tatum.
 But it wasn’t an easy aftermath for Stevens. His Instagram account was shut down because of the number of threatening and critical messages. Even his two children were targeted online.
 It was a disappointing end to a stellar nine-year stretch that produced a championship, another Finals appearance, and resurrected a historic franchise.
